title: Audit lane L4: DETERMINISTIC CAPABILITY CORRECTNESS (independent ADR-0020 candidate audit @ b57e0fdf)
description: Independent read-only audit lane L4 of the ADR-0020 SRD candidate at exact commit b57e0fdf5a42432fee4b4bc5f6f6f46b30592e25 (pack bytes = fcc76eae). Read the eshyra-o9bd.16 design. SCOPE: Every entry in packages/core/src/rules/deterministicCapabilityInventory.ts and deterministicCapabilityLedger.ts (capabilities in force): does each declare operation, inputs, exclusions, revision/identity and residual DM interpretation truthfully against its runtime owner code; does it fail closed on unrecognized input; does its evidence exercise it (bar 6)? INDEPENDENT ADR-0020 RE-AUDIT — L4 DETERMINISTIC CAPABILITY CORRECTNESS

Repository worktree remained clean. No repository files were created/edited/formatted; no build, full verification, audit-bundle command, GitHub action, commit, push, or merge was performed. L4-F1 — BLOCKER — Consuming the last Elemental Gem in a stack erases grants already paid for by earlier units.

Bar violated: section 5.9 condition 6 (correctness of positively selected capabilities), with ADR 0020 section 3's retained resource-accounting/identity guarantees. This is the in-force use_item -> start_effect grant boundary, not a demand to implement an unselected item clause. The candidate explicitly selects Elemental Gem break-gem and its typed entity grants as green; use_item returns a distinct bind credit for each non-final stack spend and tells the DM each credit pays for exactly one start_effect bind. The public tool contract returns effects without starting them; it does not require a bind before another use.

Source: magic-item:elemental-gem, SRD p. 220, verified directly with pdftotext from the vendored PDF: 'When you use an action to break the gem, an elemental is summoned as if you had cast the conjure elemental spell, and the gem’s magic is lost.' The printed table selects Air/Earth/Fire/Water for the four gem types. Each consumed gem pays for its own elemental.

Concrete reproduction: /tmp/l4-gem-conservation.mts, run from the assigned worktree with node_modules/.bin/tsx /tmp/l4-gem-conservation.mts; recorded output /tmp/l4-gem-conservation.out. For each of blue-sapphire, yellow-diamond, red-corundum and emerald, at quantities 2 and 3 (8 cases), give_item creates the stack, every break-gem call succeeds, then the script admits distinct durable elementals and distinct concentrating casters and attempts one bind per paid use. Two successful uses issue one credit; three issue two credits. After the final use, zero credits remain and exactly one unredeemed consumption receipt remains. One start_effect can redeem that receipt; every further bind fails 'the consumption receipt ... was already redeemed ... one consumption pays for one grant'. Naming the earlier issued credit instead also fails because the destroyed-row path only accepts the final receipt. There is no time advancement or concentration-owner replacement confound. /tmp/l4-gem-stack.mts separately shows the first credit present immediately before final consumption and absent immediately after it.

Cause/evidence: packages/core/src/state/itemState.ts:3072-3079 records one receipt then calls destroyInventoryItem when quantity reaches zero; packages/core/src/state/inventoryLifecycle.ts:67-72 tombstones bindings and unconditionally voids every open bind credit; packages/core/src/state/itemGrantBinding.ts:496-504 deletes them. packages/core/src/state/activeEffects.ts:4050-4080 substitutes the one receipt for the deleted inventory row, and :4378-4380 refuses the named earlier credit on that path. The successful spends have consumed resources but their corresponding selected grants can no longer be realized. These are runtime writes, not a source representation omission.

Registry: NEW class; no exact finding-registry alias for destruction of earlier paid per-unit grant credits. sol:CAP-007 concerns qualified capability ownership and is related context, not asserted as a recurrence of that original inventory finding.

Suggested owner/fix: bounded item-grant/consumption runtime owner (successor repair under eshyra-olc5.12/eshyra-xt6m.1.1; coordinate with L5). Preserve an independently redeemable entitlement for every successfully consumed unit across final-row destruction, with exact instance/variant/operation identity and no duplicate redemption or id-reuse escape. Alternatively fail atomically before consuming another unit if the architecture deliberately forbids outstanding binds, and declare that restriction; silently losing a successful spend is not acceptable. Permanent evidence should be a generalized conservation invariant over multi-unit consumption, both bind-as-you-go and multiple-paid-uses-before-binding, retaining a real Elemental Gem case. This is proportionate to lost canonical resources; no per-color duplicate test suite is required.
L4-F2 — BLOCKER — use_item does not fail closed on unrecognized operation arguments.

Bar violated: section 5.9 condition 6's explicit fail-closed requirement. The selected use_item-v1 tool accepts operation-specific inputs advertised as validated, but unknown nested argument names are silently discarded before a successful mutation. This is a direct default-tool-registry path on the unchanged candidate, not malformed pack injection.

Concrete reproduction: /tmp/l4-useitem-unknown-args.mts, runnable with node_modules/.bin/tsx /tmp/l4-useitem-unknown-args.mts. Three fresh in-memory campaigns each open combat, begin pc-1's turn, give and hold magic-item:rope-of-entanglement, and call entangle-creature. Control args {transitionOutcome:'failure'} succeed and keep machineState loose. Misspelled args {transitionOutome:'failure'} also succeed, consume the character's action, and persist machineState restraining with transition.outcome success. Control-plus-unknown {transitionOutcome:'failure',unknownPredicate:true} also succeeds and spends the action instead of refusing the unrecognized input. A sibling probe in /tmp/l4-boundary.mts supplies Bag of Tricks args {costs:{uses:0},unknown:'garbage'}; it succeeds, spends one use, rolls a creature, and issues a credit. These prove ignored inputs on both state-transition and fixed-economy branches.

Code: packages/core/src/orchestrator/toolUseItem.ts:53-57 gives args only an open object schema and describes 'Operation-specific validated inputs'; :100-105 forwards it. packages/core/src/state/itemState.ts:1735-1744 reads only transitionOutcome and defaults an absent recognized key to success; :1901-1915 reads only the current variable economy key or ignores costs entirely for a fixed cost. No args-key allowlist or operation-specific unknown-cost-key rejection runs. The recognized failure path itself works; the defect is accepting unrecognized input while committing a default outcome.

Source context: magic-item:rope-of-entanglement, SRD p. 241, checked against the vendored PDF: 'The target must succeed on a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw or become restrained.' The candidate correctly leaves the save and applying the creature condition to the DM, and represents the declared item-state failure branch. This finding does not ask the engine to adjudicate that save; it requires rejection of an unrecognized declaration rather than silently recording the success branch.

Registry: NEW class; no exact canonical alias for open use_item argument acceptance. Do not conflate it with the retired/narrowed global audit-readiness-gate claim.

Suggested owner/fix: use_item/itemState runtime owner, with the provider-neutral input-schema boundary. Validate the complete recognized operation-specific argument shape and applicable economy keys before action, economy, timer, credit or RNG work; refuse unknown names and arguments inapplicable to the selected operation. Preserve omission defaults that are deliberately supported. Permanent evidence: a generalized unknown-argument refusal invariant that checks state and budgets remain unchanged, with one state-machine and one economy-backed real-pack case, plus positive declared-input controls. This is proportionate to a live canonical mutation boundary.
L4-F3 — NON-BLOCKER — Prototype-inherited keys bypass the capability ledger's unknown-identity checks.

Relevant bar/invariant: condition 6's positive-identity/fail-closed principle and the ledger constructor's stated rejection of unknown contracts. This is a latent metadata-construction defect, not a demonstrated wrong positive capability in the candidate's eight current bindings.

Evidence: /tmp/l4-inventory.mts shows requireRuleDeterministicCapabilityContract('constructor') and ('toString') return functions and ('__proto__') returns an object instead of throwing, while an ordinary unknown string correctly throws. DETERMINISTIC_CAPABILITY_LEDGER.lookup('__proto__') returns not-positively-selected with disposition {} instead of no-statement. /tmp/l4-boundary.mts shows createDeterministicCapabilityLedger(undefined,[{ruleKey:'rule:ability-checks',capability:'constructor'}],{}) succeeds and lookup returns outcome bound with bindings [Function: Object], which has no declared operation/revision/inputs. All are read-only calls. Code locations: packages/core/src/rules/deterministicCapabilityLedger.ts:186-191, :323-327, :350-359 use inherited property lookups instead of own-key membership.

Severity/consumer boundary: the live singleton uses fixed valid revisions and prefixed corpus record keys; no current binding selects these inherited names, and no model tool exposes registry construction. Therefore this does not block this candidate re-freeze on its own. It should be repaired before admitting caller-built ledger registries or generalizing identity inputs. No SRD page applies to this software identity contract. Registry: NEW, no exact alias. Suggested owner: runtime ledger maintainer/successor to eshyra-o9bd.19.5.12. Fix with own-key membership or null-prototype dictionaries/Map; proportionate permanent evidence is one generalized inherited-key refusal test covering contract lookup, constructor binding validation, and no-statement lookup. Existing broad inventory closure tests do not cover it.

LIMITS AND NON-CLAIMS

The 115-entry declaration census, four-contract/eight-binding ledger census, and 95-evidence-file test enumeration are bounded complete populations of those artifacts. They do not establish branch-complete runtime correctness. I did not independently re-read every branch of all 200 owner files; deep adversarial source tracing was concentrated on the mutation/pack-consumption families listed above. The other engine entries, including checkpoint/replay/migrations, character creation/continuity/level-up, campaign/session lifecycle and world/ruling writes, received declaration/evidence and selected-code checks, not an exhaustive independent lifecycle or filesystem adversarial campaign. Their passing tests are evidence, not universal certification.

Custom real-pack probes explicitly enumerate: 4 Elemental Gem types x 2 stack sizes; 3 Rope of Entanglement argument shapes; 1 Bag of Tricks unknown-argument use; ordinary unknown and inherited ledger identity lookups/constructor input; and a two-item/two-dawn recharge ordering comparison. The last comparison changes seeded draw attribution when an interval is split, but I did not establish an applicable cross-item call-partition-equivalence requirement; it is not promoted to a finding. A direct malformed-readiness-record probe returned without refusing an unknown readiness enum, but that probe bypasses the contract's trusted-record input requirement; I do not claim a malformed candidate record or live candidate mutation from it. Neither observation is counted as a blocker.

Source checking was bounded to the printed p. 220 Elemental Gem and p. 241 Rope passages relevant to the runtime findings, not a corpus source-fidelity audit. I did not run pack regeneration/reproducibility (L1's concern), the audit bundle, full worktree verification, a live-play model session, or the other lanes' discovery/adjudication/state-integrity populations. Existing candidate disclosures (unselected engine-pending clauses, generic operation.excludes enforcement, Pipes variable-spend reachability, undecided roll-evidence binding, and inactive freeze hashes/guard) were not relabeled as new defects. Missing typed projections with truthful DM-adjudication boundaries were not counted as defects.

Result: two concrete in-force capability blockers, one latent non-blocker. The rest of the lane is not claimed complete or defect-free. Findings and limits are recorded only in eshyra-o9bd.16.4 for Captain consolidation; no other bead was modified.
LANE RESULT: BLOCKERS (2)
